segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Panel 5 looked similar on the face of it, so when the contractor asked whether to reuse that pattern or commission something new, I specified the Panel 3 pattern. There was exploration data showing different joint orientation in Panel 5 and a fault splay that Panel 3 didn't have, but the overall rock looked like the same family to me.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant transfers a personally successful Panel 3 support design to Panel 5 based on surface similarity while discounting case-specific exploration evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: He was under an unsupported section of back when it came down, and that's a positioning call he makes every shift. That's the part of the incident that was directly within his control, so that's where I put the emphasis in the report. It was noted, but the more immediate explanation was where the loader was actually sitting at the time. That's the piece that was in front of me and easiest to point to.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant foregrounds the operator's behavior and downweights the available elevated-joint-density ground-condition explanation when attributing the fall of ground.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, that's just how we've always operated. A single seismic event with convergence a bit above average isn't unusual for that ground — we get blips like that periodically and the standard approach has always been to keep the cycle running unless something more definitive shows up. Stopping the schedule every time there's a minor signal would grind the whole panel transition to a halt, and that's not how we do things here.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant justifies continuing the pre-existing schedule primarily by established practice and normal operating procedure despite new seismic and convergence information.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: It's a specific number, calculated from our stability model, and it cleared our standard threshold. That gave me something concrete to point to when the manager needed an answer. As for the spalling reports, minor spalling happens periodically in that ground and doesn't usually change the overall picture. On top of that, I've managed plenty of ground issues before — if something came up post-blast, I was confident we could respond and adjust support on the fly. That's part of why I felt comfortable saying go rather than waiting out the review.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant treats the 1.42 model output as a concrete sufficient basis despite mismatched calibration and spalling, and separately relies on confidence in personal ability to manage future ground issues.

candidates.details: The candidate identifies a plausible numeric-focal-point explanation and quotes the correct segment, but its stated mechanism does not fully capture the hidden model-validity distortion.

high_only.detection_interpretation: No identified finding is high confidence; all four positive segments are missed.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Moderate findings detect the support-design, incident-attribution, and final-approval segments; the low-confidence schedule finding remains excluded.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All four positive segments are detected when low-confidence identified findings are included.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Candidate inclusion does not change segment detection because the candidate is localized to an already detected positive segment.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: Full mechanism overlap with the Experience Bias instance, but the label is a similarity-based near neighbor rather than an approved equivalent.
Full mechanism overlap with the Attribution Bias instance, but the label is a narrower near neighbor rather than an approved equivalent.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly states that no retrieved scientific corpus passages were supplied, uses empty corpus_evidence arrays, and makes no unverifiable citation claims. The candidate likewise contains no retrieved-support claim.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding moderate-confidence findings changes segment detection from 0/4 to 3/4 and mechanism-first instance F1 from 0.0000 to 0.7500, while strict instance F1 reaches 0.2500.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: Adding the low-confidence Status quo finding changes segment detection from 3/4 to 4/4, strict instance F1 from 0.2500 to 0.4444, and mechanism-first F1 from 0.7500 to 0.8889.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Adding the Anchoring candidate leaves segment detection unchanged, adds one mechanism-first and one strict false positive, and reduces mechanism-first F1 from 0.8889 to 0.8000 and strict F1 from 0.4444 to 0.4000.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the RAG detects 3 of 4 positive reasoning segments with no observable false alarms; including low-confidence findings detects all 4.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, strict identification is 1 TP, 4 FN, and 2 FP (F1 0.2500); at all identified confidence levels it is 2 TP, 3 FN, and 2 FP (F1 0.4444).
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, mechanism-first identification is 3 TP and 2 FN with no FP (F1 0.7500); including low-confidence findings gives 4 TP and 1 FN (F1 0.8889).
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The single candidate is a correctly localized but partial-mechanism near miss; it is not promoted to a true positive and adds one false positive at the candidate-inclusive threshold.
main_failure_modes: The RAG did not identify the hidden Illusion of validity instance as a separate occurrence.

It used near-neighbor labels Representativeness heuristic and Fundamental attribution error instead of the benchmark labels Experience Bias and Attribution Bias, reducing strict scores despite full mechanism matches.
The exact Status quo finding was assigned low confidence and is missed at the recommended high_and_moderate threshold.
The candidate Anchoring effect is plausible but insufficiently evidenced and lowers candidate-inclusive precision.
main_strengths: All four identified findings localize to the correct positive segments with valid quotations.
The RAG captures the full mechanisms for the Experience Bias, Attribution Bias, Status quo bias, and Overconfidence Bias instances under the mechanism-first scorecard.
The Overconfidence effect label is an approved equivalent of Overconfidence Bias.
The output explicitly discloses unavailable retrieval support and preserves plausible non-bias counterinterpretations.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong segment-level sensitivity when low-confidence findings are admitted and strong mechanism-level performance at moderate confidence, but materially weaker strict taxonomy performance because two correct mechanisms receive near-neighbor labels and the model-validity instance is missed. Candidate inclusion provides no recall gain and introduces one false positive.
